html:
A copy of the Diamond Sutra, a Buddhist scripture, printed in Tang China in 868. It is the oldest printed book that carries a date.

The book is a scroll about five metres long, made of sheets of paper printed from carved wooden blocks and pasted together. It opens with a fine picture of the Buddha preaching. A note at the end says that one Wang Jie had it made for free distribution on behalf of his parents, on a date that equals 11 May 868. The skill of the cutting shows that woodblock printing was already mature by then.

It was found in 1900 in a sealed cave library at the Mogao caves near Dunhuang, among tens of thousands of manuscripts. In 1907 the explorer Aurel Stein bought it with many others and took it to London, where it is now in the British Library. China's printing ran far ahead of Europe's: Gutenberg printed with metal type almost six centuries later.
sum: A copy of the Diamond Sutra, a Buddhist scripture, printed in Tang China in 868. It is the oldest printed book that carries a date.
